title: Primitive Doctors: Decalogue is the moral-natural sum—only the Sabbath’s seventh-day rigor is ceremonial
source_text: XXIII. Unde est quod Prisci Ecclesiae Doctores communi consensu affirmant Decalogum nihil aliud continere, quam brevem summam legis Moralis atque naturalis, ad cujus observationem omnes communiter tenentur, excepto solum praecepto de sanctificatione Sabbati, seu diei septimi; in quo observarunt aliquid esse ceremoniale, nempe, praecisam & rigidam diei a creatione septimae observationem, & scrupulosam in ea cessationem ab omni opere: quamvis, quoad substantiam, & quatenus certam diem solemniter Deo sanctificari jubet, etiam morale sit.
pass_a_gloss: Whence it is that the Primitive Doctors of the Church affirm by common consent that the Decalogue contains nothing else than a brief sum of the Moral and natural law, to whose observation all are commonly bound, excepting only the commandment concerning the sanctification of the Sabbath, or seventh day; in which they observed that something is ceremonial, namely, the precise and rigid observation of the seventh day from creation, and the scrupulous cessation in it from every work: although, as to substance, and inasmuch as it commands a certain day to be solemnly sanctified to God, it is also moral.
pass_b_english: Fathers read the Decalogue as the moral-natural sum binding everyone.
Only Sabbath’s exact seventh-day stoppage is ceremonial; sanctifying some solemn day remains moral.

lemmas.gloss: a brief sum of the Moral law

choices.english: the Primitive Doctors of the Church
